newsitem.title: USA: Brookhaven national lab operator dismissed - NYTimes.
newsitem.headline: Brookhaven national lab operator dismissed - NYTimes.

text.p: The nonprofit group that ran the Brookhaven National Laboratory for the U.S. Energy Department for 50 years was dismissed by the federal government, who raised safety issues, the New York Times said Friday.

The Energy Department, which owns the Upton, N.Y. laboratory, released a report that said Brookhaven's managers felt money spent on environmental safety could have instead been spent on scientific research, the newspaper said.
According to the report, safety took a back seat within that sort of environment, the paper said.

Brookhaven was managed by contractor Associated Universities Inc, which has a governing board of scientists from 24 universities, the Times said. These universities were not affiliated with the lab, it said.
The Times said four days ago, Associated Universities named a new management team to work on safety and health issues, led by Lyle Schwartz as interim director.
Schwartz was quoted in the newspaper as saying he was "sobered but not surprised" by the action and would help with a transition.

The government report cited the laboratory's inefficient and tardy response to underground water containing low-level radioactive tritium that was believed to have leaked from Brookhaven's nuclear reactor, the paper said.
It also alleged the Energy Department had not adequately overseen the Brookhaven operation, the Times said.

At a news conference in Upton, Energy Secretary Federico Pena was quoted as saying: "There need not -- and will not -- be a tradeoff between award-winning scientific research and environment, safety and health."
An Energy Department official would be named an interim director of the facility while another would have 30 days to file a report recommending steps to correct the situation.
